Also, MT-ES is only marginally better than MT-FI in both Spanish test sets, even if it corresponds to the Translate-Train approach, whereas MT-FI needs to Zero-Shot transfer from Finnish into Spanish. answer: Examples of these artifacts include spurious patterns in NLI datasets such as SNLI and MultiNLI, where hypotheses-only baselines perform better than chance due to lexical choices and sentence lengths, and models tend to predict entailment for sentence pairs with high lexical overlap [E2]. Another example is the bias in the predictions of NLI models in the XNLI development set, where the Orig system is strongly biased towards underpredicting entailment and overpredicting neutral, especially for non-English languages, likely due to the fact that the English test set is original while the rest are human-translated [E3].
